content.text:
I have what I need. Let me confirm the key analysis before submitting.

**Analysis:**

1. **The only Customer-side minimum** is in §5(a) (p0045): fees "not less than $\_\_\_\_ per month for the Hosting Services and $\_\_\_\_ per month for Support Services" — a monthly floor, not an annual volume commitment.
2. **Term** (p0078): 1 year, auto-renewing for successive one-year periods, with either party able to give 30 days' notice of non-renewal — so no multi-year lock-in.
3. **Exit** (p0079, §14): Client may elect to terminate at any time by written notice, with services (and therefore the monthly minimums) running only to the last day of the following month — an at-will exit on roughly 30 days' notice.
4. **No shortfall/penalty mechanic** anywhere: no acceleration, no take-or-pay true-up penalty, and §2(a) (p0022) confirms Client "is not obligated to utilize the License."

This is a commitment capped at the current 12-month term, terminable on ~30 days' notice, with no shortfall penalty — squarely the fallback position, so no redline.

input.quote: a. Client will pay TrueLink's fees for requested Hosting Services and Support Services pursuant to the schedule of charges set forth on Exhibits "A" and "B" attached hereto, (but not less than $____ per month for the Hosting Services and $____ per month for Support Services).
input.rationale: The only minimum commitment imposed on Client is the monthly fee floor in § 5(a) (p0045) for Hosting and Support Services. That commitment sits at our fallback position rather than the preferred usage-only position, and is therefore acceptable without redline: (i) it is bounded by a one-year term that auto-renews only in successive one-year periods, with either party able to stop renewal on 30 days' notice (p0078); (ii) Client has a standalone at-will exit under § 14, where services — and hence the monthly minimums — run only to the last day of the month following Client's termination notice (p0079), i.e. roughly a 30-day exit; and (iii) there is no shortfall penalty, acceleration, or take-or-pay mechanic anywhere in the document, and § 2(a) expressly confirms Client "is not obligated to utilize the License" (p0022). No multi-year take-or-pay or volume cap on Client usage exists, so walk-away territory is not engaged. Two minor points noted but not flagged as deviations: the § 14 exit is stated as "Subject to Section 4," and § 4 is TrueLink's own commitment to supply a programmer "for a period of not less than ____ months," which could be argued to hold the Support Services minimum open past termination — the blank is unfilled and § 4 reads as a vendor-side obligation benefiting us, so we would clarify only if that blank is completed with a long period. Separately, § 6 (p0047) carves the minimum monthly fees out of Client's documentation and dispute rights, which is a billing-transparency point for the audit/disputes rule rather than a minimum-commitment failure. The requirement in § 3(i) (p0042) that Client order a credit report per underwriting approval is a requirements/exclusivity term addressed under that rule, not double-flagged here.
